title: “Left-Wing” Childishness and the Petty-Bourgeois Mentality
author: V.I. Lenin
context: Written in May 1918 during the fierce debate over the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk and Soviet economic policy, V.I. Lenin replies to the 'Left Communist' faction (including Nikolai Bukharin, Valerian Osinsky, and Karl Radek) and their journal Kommunist. Lenin exposes how ultra-left revolutionary phrase-making masks petty-bourgeois vacillation and a failure to grasp the concrete material tasks of transitioning from capitalism to socialism.
relatesToToday: Lenin's distinction between simple confiscation ('taking over' assets by decree) and genuine socialization (establishing nationwide accounting, disciplined organization, and mastery of large-scale production) remains essential for understanding how socialist states navigate transitional economies, state capitalism, and imperialist encirclement.
keyTakeaways: Marxist strategy requires strictly calculating the objective balance of class and military forces rather than indulging in subjective 'Left' phrase-making.
Confiscation requires only political determination, whereas true socialization requires nationwide accounting, control, and organizational mastery.
In a predominantly small-peasant economy, petty-bourgeois profiteering and anarchy of small ownership are the primary internal enemies of socialism.
State capitalism under a proletarian Soviet state is not a betrayal of socialism, but a vital transitional rung toward large-scale socialist production.
A revolutionary proletarian state must not hesitate to employ and learn from bourgeois technical specialists under strict working-class supervision.
